passage:
A city placed a large modern sculpture in front of the library. Some residents loved it. Others said it looked like twisted metal and wasted money.
The city held a public talk with the artist. She explained that the sculpture represented pages opening in the wind.
After hearing this, some people still disliked it, but they understood the idea better.
Students learned that public art belongs to everyone in feeling, even if not everyone likes it.
Disagreement does not always mean failure. Public art can make people ask what a place should express.
A sculpture may stand silently, but the conversations around it can become part of its purpose.
